intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that split-hand/foot malformation-6 (SHFM6) is caused by homozygous mutation in the WNT10B gene (601906) on chromosome 12q13.12.

checks.claim: Split-hand/foot malformation-6 (SHFM6) is caused by homozygous mutation in the WNT10B gene.
checks.evidence_quote: a homozygous missense WNT10b mutation (p.R332W) in all affected individuals but the atypical case plus in an asymptomatic female
checks.explanation: The paper reports a homozygous WNT10B mutation causing autosomal recessive SHFM. The SHFM6 label is standard nomenclature.

checks.claim: The WNT10B gene is located on chromosome 12q13.12.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified by homozygosity mapping a novel SHFM locus at 12q13.11-q13
checks.explanation: The chromosomal location is standard nomenclature and fits the mapped locus. The abstract gives only the region 12q13.11-q13, not band 12q13.12.

paragraphs.text: Split-hand/foot malformation (SHFM) affects the central rays of the hands and/or feet. Gül and Oktenli (2002) described it as characterized by absence of the central digital rays, a deep median cleft, and syndactyly of the remaining digits, and noted variable expression of the malformation pattern within families. Elliott and Evans (2006) noted that SHFM shows reduced penetrance. SHFM6 is the autosomal recessive form caused by mutation in WNT10B (Ugur and Tolun, 2008).

checks.claim: Split-hand/foot malformation (SHFM) affects the central rays of the hands and/or feet.
checks.evidence_quote: Split hand and foot malformation syndrome (SHFM) is characterized by the absence of the central digital rays
checks.explanation: The abstract defines SHFM, a malformation of the hand and foot, by absence of the central digital rays, so it affects the central rays.

checks.claim: Gül and Oktenli (2002) described SHFM as characterized by absence of the central digital rays.
checks.evidence_quote: Split hand and foot malformation syndrome (SHFM) is characterized by the absence of the central digital rays
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: Gül and Oktenli (2002) described SHFM as characterized by a deep median cleft.
checks.evidence_quote: is characterized by the absence of the central digital rays, deep median cleft, and syndactyly of the remaining digits
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: Gül and Oktenli (2002) described SHFM as characterized by syndactyly of the remaining digits.
checks.evidence_quote: is characterized by the absence of the central digital rays, deep median cleft, and syndactyly of the remaining digits
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: Gül and Oktenli (2002) noted variable expression of the SHFM malformation pattern within families.
checks.evidence_quote: A variable intrafamilial expression of the malformation pattern is apparent.
checks.explanation: The paper reports variable expression within the single inbred kindred it studied. 'Within families' is a fair rewording of 'intrafamilial'.

checks.claim: Elliott and Evans (2006) noted that SHFM shows reduced penetrance.
checks.evidence_quote: SHFM can occur as an isolated malformation or in association with other malformations, as in the ectrodactyly-ectodermal dysplasia-clefting (EEC) syndrome and other autosomal dominant conditions with long bone involvement, all showing variable expressivity and reduced penetrance.
checks.explanation: The abstract states that SHFM shows reduced penetrance.

checks.claim: SHFM6 is the autosomal recessive form of SHFM caused by mutation in WNT10B.
checks.evidence_quote: This is the first reported WNT10b mutation on the pathogenesis of limb development and recessive mutation in SHFM.
checks.explanation: The paper describes autosomal recessive SHFM caused by a WNT10B mutation.

paragraphs.text: SHFM6 is inherited as an autosomal recessive trait. Ugur and Tolun (2008) studied a large consanguineous kindred with autosomal recessive SHFM and found a homozygous WNT10B mutation. They described the inheritance as complex. The phenotype varied among affected members: most had central foot reductions with or without hand involvement, and 1 had a milder, atypical form of SHFM.

checks.claim: SHFM6 is inherited as an autosomal recessive trait.
checks.evidence_quote: We studied a large consanguineous kindred afflicted with autosomal recessive SHFM.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Ugur and Tolun (2008) studied a large consanguineous kindred with autosomal recessive SHFM.
checks.evidence_quote: We studied a large consanguineous kindred afflicted with autosomal recessive SHFM.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Ugur and Tolun (2008) found a homozygous WNT10B mutation in a large consanguineous kindred with autosomal recessive SHFM.
checks.evidence_quote: by subsequent candidate gene approach a homozygous missense WNT10b mutation (p.R332W) in all affected individuals
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Ugur and Tolun (2008) described the inheritance of SHFM in the consanguineous kindred as complex.
checks.evidence_quote: Homozygous WNT10b mutation and complex inheritance in Split-Hand/Foot Malformation.
checks.explanation: The paper's title calls the inheritance complex.

checks.claim: The SHFM phenotype varied among affected members of the kindred studied by Ugur and Tolun (2008).
checks.evidence_quote: Twelve affected members had central feet reductions with or without hand involvement while the remaining one had the mildest phenotype and atypical SHFM.
checks.explanation: The phenotype is described as varying among affected members.

checks.claim: Most affected members of the kindred studied by Ugur and Tolun (2008) had central foot reductions with or without hand involvement.
checks.evidence_quote: Twelve affected members had central feet reductions with or without hand involvement while the remaining one had the mildest phenotype
checks.explanation: Twelve of 13 affected members is most.

checks.claim: One affected member of the kindred studied by Ugur and Tolun (2008) had a milder, atypical form of SHFM.
checks.evidence_quote: the remaining one had the mildest phenotype and atypical SHFM
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

paragraphs.text: Blattner et al. (2010) found a homozygous WNT10B mutation in a patient with sporadic SHFM. They concluded that sporadic SHFM may show recessive rather than dominant inheritance.

checks.claim: Blattner et al. (2010) found a homozygous WNT10B mutation in a patient with sporadic SHFM.
checks.evidence_quote: By examining WNT10B in a patient with sporadic SHFM, we identified a homozygous 4-bp duplication resulting in a premature termination codon.
checks.explanation: The abstract directly states that a homozygous WNT10B mutation was found in a patient with sporadic SHFM.

checks.claim: Blattner et al. (2010) concluded that sporadic SHFM may show recessive rather than dominant inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: Obviously, sporadic SHFM may show recessive rather than dominant inheritance resulting in a 25% recurrence risk for sibs
checks.explanation: The abstract states this conclusion almost word for word.

paragraphs.text: Ugur and Tolun (2008) studied a large consanguineous kindred with autosomal recessive SHFM. Using homozygosity mapping, they identified a novel SHFM locus at chromosome 12q13.11-q13.

checks.claim: Ugur and Tolun (2008) studied a large consanguineous kindred with autosomal recessive SHFM.
checks.evidence_quote: We studied a large consanguineous kindred afflicted with autosomal recessive SHFM.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Using homozygosity mapping, Ugur and Tolun (2008) identified a novel SHFM locus at chromosome 12q13.11-q13.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified by homozygosity mapping a novel SHFM locus at 12q13.11-q13 with a maximum multipoint lod score of 5.47
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

paragraphs.text: SHFM is genetically heterogeneous (Elliott and Evans, 2006). Gül and Oktenli (2002) stated that most familial cases are inherited in an autosomal dominant manner. The autosomal recessive form described here results from mutation in WNT10B (Ugur and Tolun, 2008).

checks.claim: SHFM is genetically heterogeneous.
checks.evidence_quote: genetic heterogeneity, with at least five loci identified to date, further complicates management of affected patients and their families.
checks.explanation: The abstract states that SHFM is genetically heterogeneous, with at least five loci identified.

checks.claim: Gül and Oktenli (2002) stated that most familial cases of SHFM are inherited in an autosomal dominant manner.
checks.evidence_quote: The majority of the familial cases are inherited in an autosomal dominant manner.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: The autosomal recessive form of SHFM (SHFM6) results from mutation in WNT10B.
checks.evidence_quote: This is the first reported WNT10b mutation on the pathogenesis of limb development and recessive mutation in SHFM.
checks.explanation: The paper reports that the autosomal recessive SHFM in this kindred results from a WNT10B mutation.

paragraphs.text: In a large consanguineous kindred with autosomal recessive SHFM mapped to 12q13, Ugur and Tolun (2008) identified a homozygous missense mutation in the WNT10B gene (R332W) by a candidate gene approach. The mutation was present in all affected individuals except the 1 with an atypical phenotype. It was also present in an asymptomatic female.

checks.claim: The autosomal recessive SHFM in the large consanguineous kindred studied by Ugur and Tolun (2008) mapped to chromosome 12q13.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified by homozygosity mapping a novel SHFM locus at 12q13.11-q13
checks.explanation: The locus maps to the 12q13 region.

checks.claim: Ugur and Tolun (2008) identified a homozygous missense mutation in WNT10B (R332W) in a large consanguineous kindred with autosomal recessive SHFM.
checks.evidence_quote: a homozygous missense WNT10b mutation (p.R332W) in all affected individuals
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Ugur and Tolun (2008) identified the WNT10B R332W mutation by a candidate gene approach.
checks.evidence_quote: by subsequent candidate gene approach a homozygous missense WNT10b mutation (p.R332W)
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: The WNT10B R332W mutation was present in all affected individuals of the kindred except the 1 with an atypical phenotype.
checks.evidence_quote: in all affected individuals but the atypical case plus in an asymptomatic female
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: The WNT10B R332W mutation was also present in an asymptomatic female of the kindred.
checks.evidence_quote: in all affected individuals but the atypical case plus in an asymptomatic female
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

paragraphs.text: Blattner et al. (2010) examined WNT10B in a patient with sporadic SHFM and identified a homozygous nonsense mutation. This finding was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.

checks.claim: Blattner et al. (2010) examined the WNT10B gene in a patient with sporadic SHFM.
checks.evidence_quote: By examining WNT10B in a patient with sporadic SHFM, we identified a homozygous 4-bp duplication
checks.explanation: The abstract says the authors examined WNT10B in a patient with sporadic SHFM.

checks.claim: Blattner et al. (2010) identified a homozygous nonsense mutation in WNT10B in a patient with sporadic SHFM.
checks.evidence_quote: Homozygous nonsense mutation in WNT10B and sporadic split-hand/foot malformation (SHFM) with autosomal recessive inheritance.
checks.explanation: The title calls it a homozygous nonsense mutation. The abstract describes it as a 4-bp duplication that creates a premature termination codon, which is consistent with the title's wording.

checks.claim: The homozygous WNT10B nonsense mutation in the patient with sporadic SHFM was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: Nine heterozygous relatives show no sign of SHFM.
checks.explanation: The title links the mutation to 'autosomal recessive inheritance', and the nine unaffected heterozygous relatives support a recessive pattern.
